newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian youth seen facing bleak job market.
newsitem.headline: Canadian youth seen facing bleak job market.

text.p: The number of Canadian young people with jobs dropped steeply in recent years, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
The employment rate for Canadians aged 15 to 24 in 1996 was 51.1 percent, a drop of more than 11 percentage points since 1989, the federal agency said.
"The labor market has become a more precarious place for young people in the 1990s," the agency said in its spring 1997 report on youth unemployment, a persistent problem in Canada.
The number of young people actively looking for jobs also dropped sharply, declining more than 10 percentage points from 1989 to 61.2 percent.
The youth unemployment rate of 16.1 percent in 1996 was almost double that of 8.5 percent for the general population, Statscan said.
The agency said that the percentage of young people working part time more than doubled in the past two decades, climbing to 46 percent in 1996 from 21 percent in 1976.
Fewer students were also finding summer jobs. In July 1996, 52 percent of young people had summer jobs, down from 69 percent in July 1989.
